choices.content: Snakes that can add are purple.

question.prompt:
Tom has a collection of \(13\) snakes, \(4\) of which are purple and \(5\) of which are happy. He observes that

• all of his happy snakes can add,

• none of his purple snakes can subtract, and

• all of his snakes that can’t subtract also can’t add.

Which of these conclusions can be drawn about Tom’s snakes?

solutions.explanation:
Start with a purple snake. It cannot subtract, and the third observation then says it cannot add. But every happy snake can add. A snake cannot both be unable to add and be a happy snake that can add.

Thus no happy snake is purple, so the justified conclusion is D.

The important direction is the chain from purple to unable to subtract to unable to add. The observations do not let us reverse every implication; for example, they do not say that every snake that can add is happy.
solutions.title: Chain the stated implications without reversing them.
